title: Prototype optional BLAS-backed GF(251) cascade (615db3b9 Phase 1 route B)
description:
Phase 1 route B of the finite-field LA SOTA catch-up plan (`dev/active/615db3b9-finite-field-la-sota-plan.md` § Phase 1, item 2). Implements or prototypes an optional BLAS-backed GF(251) cascade — feature-gated, not enabled in the default build — so the route can be compared head-to-head against route A (in-Rust f32/FMA) and route C (integer panel) before route selection. Parent epic: 026fc832. Predecessor: 615db3b9 (plan, done). ## Background The plan's Phase 1, item 2 says: "Implement or prototype an optional `blas`/`external-blas` feature, or an out-of-tree benchmark harness, that packs `Fp

` to f32 and calls a single-threaded `sgemm` provider. This is the closest apples-to-apples fflas route. It should not become a default dependency without explicit user approval." The route does not commit gf2-core to a BLAS dependency in the default build. The deliverable is evidence — whether a single-threaded `sgemm`-backed cascade clears the fflas-ffpack performance ceiling for GF(251), and what the dependency cost would be if adopted as an optional accelerator. ## Success Criteria - [hard] Either (a) an optional `blas`/`external-blas` Cargo feature on `gf2-core` (or `gf2-algebra` / a new prototype crate, per dispatch decision) that wires an external single-threaded sgemm provider behind a non-default feature gate, OR (b) an out-of-tree benchmark harness under `dev/research/` that links to a single-threaded sgemm provider and runs the same fixed-seed GF(251) workload as Candidate C. Either path must be feature-gated such that the default `cargo build --workspace --all-features` on a host without the BLAS provider still succeeds. - [hard] Bit-exact equality vs the existing Candidate C output at GF(251)/n in {64, 256, 1024} on canonical seeds. - [hard] CCX-pinned 5-trial measurement at GF(251)/n in {256, 1024} on the 5900X reference host, recorded as a CSV + evidence markdown doc. - [hard] Evidence doc records the chosen BLAS provider (e.g., OpenBLAS, Intel MKL, BLIS), its threading mode (must be single-threaded for apples-to-apples), license, and a recommendation on whether to ship it as a default-off accelerator or to keep it as a reference-only benchmark. - [hard] Implementation does NOT add fflas-ffpack, Givaro, or FFPACK as a dependency anywhere. The chosen BLAS provider must be a permissively-licensed BLAS (or system BLAS through a thin abstraction). - [hard] No regression on currently-PASSing GF(p) cells (delta ≤ 5%) — by construction, since the BLAS path is non-default. - [hard] No fflas-ffpack source code, comments, or autotuning tables are copied or translated into the prototype. ## Out of scope - Enabling the BLAS feature in the default build (requires explicit user approval per `references/escalation-policy.md`). - Route A (in-Rust) or route C (integer panel) prototypes. - Multi-threaded BLAS measurement (single-threaded only for this prototype). ## Notes If the prototype demonstrates a decisive win but the in-house routes (A, C) stay below the threshold, the route-selection task records BLAS as an optional accelerator and the default build remains self-contained — see the plan's Phase 1 decision rule.
